# Self-Hosted K8s Browser Dev Workspaces for Claude Code — Analysis

Decision deliverable: which existing tool (if any) to adopt for hosting many
browser-accessible, isolated Claude Code (`claude` CLI) sessions on a 3-node HA k3s
homelab — or whether to build custom. Every factual claim is cited to
[`citations.md`](citations.md); per-dimension detail is in [`references/`](references/).

## Methodology note

Sources were gathered in two layers: WebSearch discovery + counter-discovery agents
returned URL manifests (snippet-level), then the coordinator independently **fetched**
the decision-critical primary sources (license files, official Tailscale/Longhorn/Argo
CD/Anthropic docs, key GitHub issues) and confirmed exact wording. Claims resting only
on un-fetched snippets are flagged "(Snippet)" throughout. Multi-engine (DuckDuckGo)
augmentation was deliberately skipped — the 14-agent manifest pool already gave dense
coverage and added engines meant more URLs to fetch for marginal diversity. Two
independent agents audited the written output.

## Executive summary & recommendation

**Recommendation: build-custom — code-server `StatefulSet`-per-session + a Tailscale
`LoadBalancer` (HTTP) per session on a shared ProxyGroup + Headlamp as the browser
portal + a per-session `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` Secret.** Adopt
[**kube-coder**](references/other-platforms.md) [32] as the reference/base — it already
implements per-user code-server RWO pods with Claude Code and a browser terminal —
rather than greenfielding. Validate its solo-maintenance and Tailscale/Argo CD fit
before committing.

This wins because the operator's three deliberate constraints — **HTTP-only Tailscale
(no tailnet HTTPS)**, **Longhorn RWO-only**, and **browser-only single-operator** —
penalise exactly what the team-oriented platforms assume:

1. **HTTP-only TS Operator is the silent disqualifier.** Coder's web IDEs need a
   wildcard hostname **and** wildcard TLS cert [5]; Eclipse Che assumes TLS end-to-end
   plus a mandatory OIDC provider [11][12] (Snippet-level — strong inference, not a
   demonstrated HTTP-only config). The TS Operator's `Ingress` path is HTTPS-
   only [42]. Build-custom uses a `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` **plain-HTTP** Service
   per session [42] — no TLS, no wildcard, clean.
2. **RWO-only** suits every per-session-pod model; only Che's *default* per-user
   strategy and naive multi-user code-server want RWX [8][35] — both avoidable.
3. **Single-operator browser-only** makes a full workspace control plane (Coder's
   Postgres + Terraform + mesh; Che's ~13 GiB control plane [10]) pure overhead.

If you would rather adopt a full platform than assemble one, **Coder is the heavyweight
fallback** — viable via its server-relayed HTTP dashboard with the embedded mesh bypassed
[2], but accept **web-terminal-only** (code-server-in-browser needs wildcard TLS you do
not have [5]) and a heavier Day-2 footprint. **Eclipse Che, DevPod, Kasm, Okteto,
Daytona, Gitpod, and the agent-native tools are not recommended** (reasons below).

## Per-candidate narrative

- **Coder** — [details](references/coder.md). AGPL core, Community unlimited; browser
  access is server-relayed HTTP so the embedded mesh is bypassable behind the TS Operator
  [2]; RWO template [4]. The clash: code-server web IDE needs wildcard DNS + TLS [5] you
  don't have, so you're limited to the web terminal (fine for the `claude` TUI). Heavy
  (Postgres + Terraform + mesh). Viable adopt-fallback, not the best fit.
- **Eclipse Che** — [details](references/eclipse-che.md). EPL, active; RWX **not**
  required (per-workspace RWO) [8][9]; but TLS-everywhere + mandatory OIDC [11][12] clash
  with the HTTP-only TS Operator, and the ~13 GiB control plane [10] is heavy for a
  homelab. Not recommended.
- **DevPod** — [details](references/devpod.md). MPL, but a **client-only desktop
  launcher**; the browser portal is paid DevPod Pro [15][17], failing browser-only;
  maintenance stalled [16]. Disqualified.
- **JupyterHub + KubeSpawner** — [details](references/jupyterhub-kubespawner.md). BSD,
  excellent RWO/sidecar fit [20][21], but hosting code-server is a *proxy* pattern
  [19][24] with WebSocket fragility and a past CVE [22], and the multi-user apparatus is
  overhead for one operator. Workable but awkward.
- **Other** — [details](references/other-platforms.md). **Theia Cloud** is the strongest
  k8s-native OSS portal [28][29] but Theia-IDE-centric with RWO unverified; **kube-coder**
  is the closest turnkey to the exact need (per-user code-server RWO + Claude Code +
  browser terminal) [32]; **Kasm/Okteto/Daytona/Gitpod** are disqualified (agent-outside-
  k8s / commercial / pivoted / deprecated) [26][33][30][31].
- **Agent-native** — [details](references/agent-native-platforms.md). None meets
  self-host-k8s + browser + runs-actual-`claude` + OSS at once; the ones that run real
  Claude Code are desktop (Sculptor [38]) or SaaS [39], and the k8s/browser one runs its
  own agent (OpenHands [36]).

## Why build-custom (reasoning tied to constraints)

[Cross-cutting detail and the full build-custom design](references/cross-cutting-build-vs-adopt.md).

The recommendation is not anti-platform in general — it is that **these platforms are
built for teams of human developers** (multi-tenancy, SSO, templated self-service), and
the single-operator + HTTP-only + RWO-only constraints turn their differentiators into
liabilities while leaving the actual need — a browser terminal running `claude`,
per-session isolated — trivially served by a code-server pod. The decisive facts:

1. Tailscale `LoadBalancer` plain-HTTP per session [42] sidesteps the wildcard-TLS wall
   that limits Coder [5] and the TLS/OIDC wall that blocks Che [11][12].
2. `StatefulSet` + `volumeClaimTemplates` RWO [50] is the correct Longhorn primitive and
   avoids the RollingUpdate Multi-Attach trap [43] ([50]'s ordered-termination behaviour
   is Snippet-level — confirm before relying on it for stop/start).
3. Headlamp gives browser-only start/stop/exec with little custom code [49] (its exec/scale
   specifics are Snippet-level — verify); Argo CD manages
   the chart while sessions live untracked in their own namespace [44][45].
4. The credential model (below) is identical for every option, so it is not a
   differentiator — and it specifically rewards per-session isolated PVCs [48], which the
   custom model gives natively.

## Recommended-option risks on this exact stack

1. **WebSocket over Tailscale LB Service:** code-server is WebSocket-heavy; reliability of
   long-lived WS through `loadBalancerClass: tailscale` LB Services at concurrency is
   **unverified** [42]. Test with 2–3 concurrent sessions before scaling.
2. **Per-session proxy-pod cost:** default is one proxy Pod per exposed Service [41]; use a
   pre-created multi-replica **ProxyGroup** to bound the footprint [42]. No documented hard
   ceiling on services per ProxyGroup.
3. **Longhorn Multi-Attach on node drain:** a k3s node upgrade detaches/reattaches each
   session's RWO volume (1–3 min) [43]; StatefulSet ordered termination avoids the
   RollingUpdate variant [50].
4. **Claude OAuth is the highest risk:** headless auto-refresh is broken — Cloudflare WAF
   locks out headless Linux refresh (403→429, multi-day lockout) [47] and concurrent
   sessions sharing creds invalidate each other [48]. **Use `claude setup-token` → a
   1-year `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` per session via Secret** [46], with isolated `~/.claude`
   PVCs; treat the sidecar-refresh pattern as unreliable [47]. Note the Jun 15 2026 Agent
   SDK credit change (affects `claude -p`/SDK, not interactive) [46].
5. **Argo CD orphan monitoring:** warn-only, but enable an ignore rule or a dedicated
   namespace so session resources don't generate noise [44][45].
6. **k3s NetworkPolicy:** default Flannel does not enforce NetworkPolicy [25] (Snippet) —
   per-session network isolation needs a policy-aware CNI (Calico/Cilium) regardless of
   which candidate you pick.

## Build-custom design sketch

```
Per session (anchor):  StatefulSet replicas:1
  ├─ container: code-server (integrated terminal; `claude` installed)   [4][32]
  ├─ initContainer: git clone <config repo>; reconcile ~/.claude        [50]
  ├─ sidecar (optional): credential refresh — but prefer Secret-injected
  │     CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token` (1-yr)         [46][47]
  ├─ volumeClaimTemplate: RWO PVC (Longhorn) at /home/coder             [50][8]
  └─ Service: type LoadBalancer, loadBalancerClass tailscale (HTTP),
        bound to shared ProxyGroup → http://<session>.<tailnet>.ts.net  [42]
Ephemeral session:     bare Pod, emptyDir, same Service pattern
Portal:                Headlamp (scale 0↔1 = stop/start; exec; delete)  [49]
GitOps:                Argo CD → Helm "session" chart; sessions in an
                       un-tracked namespace (no prune)                  [44][45]
```
kube-coder [32] already implements most of this — adopt/fork over greenfield.

## Limitations

- The HTTP-only-Tailscale verdicts for Coder web IDEs and Che auth rest on the
  *intersection* of fetched facts (wildcard-TLS requirement [5]; Ingress HTTPS-only [42];
  Che TLS/OIDC assumptions [11][12]) — no source tested these exact products behind an
  HTTP-only TS Operator. They are strong inferences, not demonstrated configs.
- Theia Cloud's RWO/RWX storage mode is **undocumented** on fetched pages — the single
  biggest unverified fact for ranking the strongest k8s-native alternative.
- WebSocket-through-Tailscale-LB at concurrency, ProxyGroup service ceilings, and
  kube-coder production-readiness are unverified.
- Several breadth claims (Kasm 5-session cap, Okteto license split, orchestrator landscape,
  k3s Flannel NetworkPolicy) are Snippet-level — see each reference file's gaps section.
